key_insight: A tensor-efficient PI-DeepONet implementation can be mathematically equivalent to the original while dramatically cutting training cost by avoiding redundant Branch-network evaluations.
engineering_relevance: This makes physics-informed operator learning more practical for higher-dimensional PDEs, enabling faster training and previously infeasible 3D runs on limited GPU memory.
method: Remove redundancy in Branch-network inputs across collocation points
Reduce tensor sizes and the number of Branch evaluations
Analyze computational complexity and derive scaling laws for collocation points and input functions
evidence_signal: Across 1D, 2D, and 3D linear advection tests, the modified model matched predictive accuracy while reducing training time, with up to 3.75× speed-up in 2D and enabling 3D training on an A100 GPU.
watch_item: Speedups depend on careful tensor handling and implementation details, so memory layout or batching choices may erase gains if not engineered correctly.
paper_title: The importance of tensor handling and implementation of physics-informed DeepONets
